page: Microsoft Azure D2pds_v5 is an ARM-based virtual machine belonging to the DPDSv5 server family. It runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor and is powered by an Ampere Altra ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor. This configuration features 2 dedicated physical cores with 1 thread per core, operating at a clock speed of 3.0 GHz. The CPU includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 4.0 GB per core. Local storage is bundled with a 77 GB SSD, and the instance supports Premium Storage.

Benchmark data indicates that the D2pds_v5 delivers average single-core performance but struggles under multi-core and memory-intensive workloads. In stress-ng testing, single-core CPU performance reached 1822.18, categorized as average, while multi-core performance dropped to a weak rating of 3612.77. Memory bandwidth tests showed poor to weak results, with cached small-block read-only bandwidth at 140.69 GB/sec and uncached large-block write bandwidth at 15.78 GB/sec. Geekbench testing yielded a single-core score of 1107.0 and a multi-core score of 2008.0. Cryptography and physics simulations also scored poorly in Passmark evaluations.

The primary tradeoff of the D2pds_v5 is its limited multi-threaded and memory throughput capabilities, which restrict its utility for intensive computing or large-scale database operations. However, its ARM architecture and dedicated core allocation provide a stable, cost-efficient hardware profile for lightweight workloads that do not require x86 compatibility. It is suitable for basic web serving, single-threaded application testing, light software compilation, and simple background tasks.
description: Microsoft Azure D2pds_v5 is an ARM-based virtual machine from the DPDSv5 family, powered by a 3.0 GHz Ampere Altra ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor. It features 2 dedicated physical cores, 8.0 GB of RAM, and a bundled 77 GB local SSD. Operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this instance supports Premium Storage. Benchmark results show average single-core performance, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1822.18 and gzip compression speed of 24.14 GB/sec. However, multi-core and memory-intensive benchmarks are weak to poor, as evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 2008.0 and a large-block write memory bandwidth of 15.78 GB/sec. Due to these performance characteristics, the D2pds_v5 is best suited for lightweight, single-threaded workloads, basic web serving, and software development tasks that benefit from ARM architecture without requiring high memory throughput.
